messages.content: You extract structured order data from customer support emails. Reply with a single JSON object that validates against the JSON schema given in the user message. Use null for any field the email does not state; never guess. Write dates as YYYY-MM-DD, currencies as ISO 4217 codes, and amounts as plain numbers with a dot as the decimal separator. Keep names exactly as written. The email may be in any language. Do not wrap the JSON in markdown and do not add any commentary. The email is provided as raw headers plus body. The From header contains the customer's name and email; the Date header gives the email send date, NOT the order date. Only use the Date header for order_date if the body explicitly states the order was placed on that date. Extract order_id, total_amount, and currency only from the customer's own words in the body; ignore numbers that appear in other contexts. The issue field must be one of: damaged, missing_item, wrong_item, late_delivery, billing_error, other. Choose 'other' when the email does not clearly describe one of the first five issues. If customer_name or customer_email cannot be parsed from the From header, use null.

JSON schema:
{"properties": {"order_id": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Order id such as HH-48213, null if not stated", "title": "Order Id"}, "customer_name": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Full name of the customer as written", "title": "Customer Name"}, "customer_email": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Customer's email address", "title": "Customer Email"}, "order_date": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Order date as YYYY-MM-DD, null if not stated", "title": "Order Date"}, "total_amount": {"anyOf": [{"type": "number"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "Order total as a plain number, no symbol", "title": "Total Amount"}, "currency": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. EUR", "title": "Currency"}, "issue": {"enum": ["damaged", "missing_item", "wrong_item", "late_delivery", "billing_error", "other"], "title": "Issue", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["order_id", "customer_name", "customer_email", "order_date", "total_amount", "currency", "issue"], "title": "OrderFields", "type": "object"}

Email:
From: María José García <kwame65@example.de>
To: support@helphub.example
Date: Wed, 16 Apr 2025 14:22:11 +0200
Subject: Order - late delivery??

Hello support team

I am writing because my order still not here. It was supposed to come last week on the 11th but nothing. I check tracking and it says delayed in customs since 10th April. This is very bad because I need the items for my mothers birthday on 25th.

The total I paid was 424.49 JPY on 16/04/2025. My name is María José García and email kwame65@example.de. I dont have the order number handy because the confirmation email went to spam and I deleted it by mistake. 

Please can you check with the shipping company? I want it delivered ASAP or I will need a refund.

Also I saw on your website it says 2-3 business days delivery but it has been 6 days now. This is not acceptable.

Thanks
María

P.S. I tried calling your phone number but it just rings and rings. No one answers.

order_id.description: Order id such as HH-48213, null if not stated
order_id.title: Order Id

customer_name.description: Full name of the customer as written
customer_name.title: Customer Name

order_date.description: Order date as YYYY-MM-DD, null if not stated
order_date.title: Order Date

total_amount.description: Order total as a plain number, no symbol
total_amount.title: Total Amount

message.reasoning:
We need to parse fields:

- Customer name: from From header: "María José García". So customer_name = "María José García".
- Customer email: same header: "<kwame65@example.de>" => "kwame65@example.de".

- Order ID: Not mentioned anywhere (they say they don't have order number). So null.

- Total amount: They wrote "The total I paid was 424.49 JPY on 16/04/2025." That's an amount and currency. Must extract from customer's own words. Yes. So total_amount = 424.49 (as number), currency = "JPY". Note we should ensure numeric format without commas etc.

- Order date: Need to see if they mention order date. They said "It was supposed to come last week on the 11th but nothing." Also "tracking ... delayed in customs since 10th April." And also "The total I paid was 424.49 JPY on 16/04/2025." But note instruction: Only use the Date header for order_date if the body explicitly states the order was placed on that date. Here they gave payment date maybe equals order date? They said "on 16/04/2025" which matches today's date (the email date). However they didn't explicitly say the order was placed on that date; they said they paid then. Could interpret that order placed/payment made on that date. Usually purchase occurs at payment time. Might consider that as order date. But rule: Only use the Date header for order_date if the body explicitly states the order was placed on that date. We are not using Date header anyway; we could derive order date from body statement: "The total I paid was 424.49 JPY on 16/04/2025." Does that indicate order placed? Possibly yes. Since they refer to paying total on that date, likely order placed then. There's no explicit phrase "order placed on". Safer to treat as not explicit enough? The instructions: "Only use the Date header for order_date if the body explicitly states the order was placed on that date." For extracting order date from body, there is no restriction besides needing to be stated. So we can take the date mentioned in body as order date if it indicates order date. The line mentions payment date; might be considered order date. Let's assume order_date = "2025-04-16". Format YYYY-MM-DD.

If uncertain, we could set null. But better to fill.

Now issue: The email describes late delivery ("my order still not here... supposed to come last week on the 11th but nothing... tracking delayed...") So issue = "late_delivery". Indeed.

Thus final JSON:

{
 "order_id": null,
 "customer_name": "María José García",
 "customer_email": "kwame65@example.de",
 "order_date": "2025-04-16",
 "total_amount": 424.49,
 "currency": "JPY",
 "issue": "late_delivery"
}

Check required fields all present.

Return JSON only.
